strategies.name: Detect ARP Cache Poisoning Across Linux, Windows, and macOS

analytics.name: Analytic 1091
analytics.guidance: Detects anomalous ARP traffic or cache modifications on Windows endpoints that indicate ARP poisoning. Behavioral focus is on multiple IP addresses resolving to a single MAC, or unsolicited ARP replies from unauthorized devices.

tuning.description: Expected MAC address for default gateways; deviations may indicate poisoning.
Correlation interval for repeated unsolicited ARP replies.

log_sources.name: WinEventLog:Security
log_sources.channel: ARP cache modification attempts observed through event tracing or security baselines

analytics.name: Analytic 1092
analytics.guidance: Detects suspicious gratuitous ARP responses or inconsistent IP-to-MAC mappings using auditd and packet capture. Behavioral focus is on unsolicited replies overriding legitimate ARP ownership.

tuning.description: Expected legitimate IP-to-MAC updates for servers or virtual routers.
Number of anomalous ARP packets per second before triggering detection.

log_sources.name: NSM:Flow
log_sources.channel: Gratuitous ARP replies with mismatched IP-MAC binding

analytics.name: Analytic 1093
analytics.guidance: Detects anomalous ARP cache changes and unsolicited ARP broadcasts using unified logs and packet capture. Behavioral detection includes multiple IP addresses mapped to the same MAC address and repeated gratuitous ARP traffic.

tuning.description: Known MAC addresses for gateways or DHCP servers; used to detect spoofed ARP entries.
How many ARP inconsistencies to tolerate before escalating detection.

log_sources.name: macos:unifiedlog
log_sources.channel: ARP table updates inconsistent with expected gateway or DHCP lease assignments

log_sources.name: NSM:Flow
log_sources.channel: Excessive gratuitous ARP replies on local subnet
